paper_metadata.title: Influence of temperature on mechanical behavior and plasticity mechanism of a precipitation-strengthened medium-entropy alloy

evidence.quote: This study examines the tensile behavior and plastic deformation mechanisms of the (CoCrNi) 94Ti 3Al 3 alloy at 298, 77, and 20 K using in-situ neutron diffraction and electron microscopy methods.

mechanisms.name: dislocation shearing
mechanisms.material_state: tensile-deformed to 3% engineering strain at 20 K

evidence.quote: at 20 K, the planar disloca - tions penetrate the L1 2 nanoparticles, as evidenced in Figure 8(b), suggesting that the L1 2 nanoprecipitates are likely sheared by the dislocations.

mechanisms.name: Orowan dislocation bypassing
mechanisms.material_state: aged (annealed 1373 K + aged 1073 K, water quenched)

evidence.quote: For the (CoCrNi) 94Ti 3Al 3 MEA, the σ-phase primarily strengthens the material through the dislocation bypassing mechanism, while the nanosized L1 2 particles contribute to strengthening through the dis - location shearing mechanism.
At higher tempera - tures, such as 298 K, thermally activated recovery becomes more prominent, leading to more efficient dislocation re - covery compared to lower temperatures, like 20 and 77 K.
The strain hardening rates at 77 and 20 K are much higher than those at 298 K, indicating that dislocation multiplication occurs more rapidly at cryogenic temperatures.
A larger number of dislocations and stacking faults are formed at 20 and 77 K compared to 298 K, contributing to enhanced strain-hardening capacity at cryogenic temperatures.

This capability allows the material to retain significant strain-hardening capacity even under very high levels of strain, resulting in an exceptional combination of strength and ductility at cryogenic temperatures.
